title: Mind on the Table
style: Somber breakbeat jazz with brushed drums, broken kick patterns, walking upright bass, and smoky minor-key piano accents; verse rides sparse with rim clicks and bass, pre-chorus opens into clipped horn replies, chorus lands on a looping piano figure and loose ride cymbal. Breathy close-mic vocal with doubled phrases, a few sung ad-libs, and delay throws on the hook. Reversed cymbal swells, tape-stop turns, and tiny sax flourishes between lines. Dark, intimate, and polished with a dusty late-night mix., somber, jazz, breakbeat
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You put the room on your back
Every stare felt like a pack
Every grin was a test
Every pause, a silent request

You kept score in your chest
Folded fear into a vest
But the mirror said, plain
Most of that is your own chain

[Pre-Chorus]
You been hauling names
That were never yours to claim
You been holding rain
In a glass of borrowed blame

[Chorus]
Let go, let go
It was all in your head
Let go, let go
Lay that weight down instead
No one’s holding you there
No one’s calling your name
Let go, let go
And the pressure falls away

[Verse 2]
You read the room too hard
Found a war in every card
Took a shrug like a wound
Made a storm out of noon

But the floor still holds
Even when the fear gets bold
And the hands unclench slow
That’s where the soft truth shows

[Pre-Chorus]
You been hauling names
That were never yours to claim
You been holding rain
In a glass of borrowed blame

[Chorus]
Let go, let go
It was all in your head
Let go, let go
Lay that weight down instead
No one’s holding you there
No one’s calling your name
Let go, let go
And the pressure falls away

[Bridge]
What if the fear was just a door?
What if you don’t need to earn the floor?
You can stand
You can breathe
You can leave it with the seat

[Chorus]
Let go, let go
It was all in your head
Let go, let go
Lay that weight down instead
No one’s holding you there
No one’s calling your name
Let go, let go
And the pressure falls away
